output.impression: 1. Well-defined 2.8 x 2.2 cm homogeneous anterior mediastinal soft-tissue mass with preserved fat planes, most consistent with a thymoma; no imaging evidence of invasion. 2. No lymphadenopathy, pleural nodules or effusion. Lungs clear.
Bedside respiratory function within normal limits: FVC 3.2 L (91% predicted; 53.7 mL/kg), no supine fall, MIP -72 cmH2O, MEP 94 cmH2O, strong cough.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right MRD1 improves by 2.5 mm after 2 minutes of ice
action_criteria.label: Perform a bedside ice-pack test on the ptotic eyelid
action_criteria.rationale: Bilateral ptosis, right worse, is present; improvement of at least 2 mm after ice supports a neuromuscular junction cause at the bedside.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Anti-AChR binding 4.2 nmol/L with elevated blocking and modulating antibodies; TSH and free T4 normal
action_criteria.label: Order AChR binding antibody and thyroid function
action_criteria.rationale: AChR binding antibody is the first-line serology for fatigable ptosis, diplopia and proximal weakness and separates MG from an MS relapse; thyroid function screens for associated autoimmune thyroid disease (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Decrement of 14% in deltoid and 18% in nasalis at 3 Hz with normal baseline CMAPs and no significant post-exercise increment
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation including a facial and a proximal muscle
action_criteria.rationale: RNS at 2-3 Hz in clinically weak facial and proximal muscles confirms a postsynaptic transmission defect and, with normal baseline CMAPs and no increment, argues against LEMS (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No new T2/FLAIR or gadolinium-enhancing lesion and no imaging features of PML; MS lesions unchanged
action_criteria.label: Order gadolinium brain MRI to exclude MS activity and PML
action_criteria.rationale: On natalizumab with a JCV index of 3.1 and new eye findings, MS relapse and natalizumab-associated PML must be excluded; here brain MRI answers the mimics the case raises, not the MG diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Increased jitter and blocking in orbicularis oculi
action_criteria.label: Single-fibre EMG only if the diagnosis were still open
action_criteria.rationale: With positive AChR antibodies and a diagnostic RNS decrement, SFEMG adds no diagnostic information; it is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Well-defined 2.8 x 2.2 cm homogeneous anterior mediastinal mass consistent with thymoma, without invasion
action_criteria.label: Order mediastinal CT with contrast for thymoma
action_criteria.rationale: Every patient with MG needs thymic imaging; a thymoma is an indication for thymectomy regardless of MG severity (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance; Sanders 2016).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC 3.2 L (91% predicted, 53.7 mL/kg), MIP -72 cmH2O, MEP 94 cmH2O
action_criteria.label: Measure baseline respiratory function
action_criteria.rationale: Generalized MG with jaw fatigue and planned thymectomy: a baseline FVC, MIP and MEP stages respiratory reserve before surgery and immunotherapy (Lawn 2001 thresholds).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Natalizumab combined with corticosteroid or azathioprine immunosuppression raises PML risk; TPMT before azathioprine
action_criteria.label: Check her medications against the MG treatment plan
action_criteria.rationale: She is on natalizumab with a high anti-JCV index, so adding MG immunosuppression is a real interaction that changes the order of treatment: natalizumab has to be replaced before a steroid-sparing agent is started.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published guidance on MG management and on natalizumab PML risk
action_criteria.label: Optionally review published guidance on MG management
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.

Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.
Do not attribute fatigable ptosis, diplopia or bulbar weakness to an MS relapse or a functional cause before AChR antibody testing and neurophysiology.
Do not add azathioprine, mycophenolate or another steroid-sparing immunosuppressant while natalizumab continues (PML risk).
required_recommendations: Start pyridostigmine 30-60 mg three to five times daily, titrated to effect (maximum about 360-480 mg/day).

If symptoms are not controlled, add prednisone at a low dose (10-20 mg/day) increased slowly, because she worsened after the recent IV methylprednisolone course; start a steroid-sparing agent (azathioprine after TPMT testing) only after natalizumab has been stopped (Sanders 2016).

Refer to thoracic surgery for thymectomy of the 2.8 cm anterior mediastinal mass (thymoma), with pre-operative IVIG or plasma exchange only if bulbar or respiratory weakness becomes significant; tell the anaesthetist about MG (reduced non-depolarising neuromuscular blocker doses with quantitative monitoring).

Plan with her MS neurologist to stop natalizumab (anti-JCV index 3.1 after about 3 years: high PML risk, increased further by MG immunosuppression) and switch to an alternative disease-modifying therapy without a long gap, for example an anti-CD20 agent; avoid alemtuzumab and interferon beta, after which MG onset or worsening has been reported.
Give her a list of drugs that can worsen MG (fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, IV magnesium, beta-blockers) and advise urgent review for dysphagia or breathlessness.

avoided_actions.rationale: No seizure or encephalopathy; EEG has no role in a neuromuscular junction disorder (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).
Gadolinium MRI shows no new or atypical lesion, so neither CSF JCV PCR nor oligoclonal bands would change management; CSF has no role in MG (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).
FDG-PET is not indicated in MG; contrast CT characterizes the anterior mediastinal mass for surgery.
No cardiac symptom, murmur or arrhythmia; echocardiography is not part of the MG work-up.
No palpitations, syncope or arrhythmia; cardiac monitoring is not part of the MG work-up.

accepted: Myasthenia gravis, AChR antibody-positive, generalized (MGFA Class IIb), with thymoma, concurrent with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis on natalizumab

differential.key_features: Gadolinium MRI shows no new T2 or enhancing lesion and the prior right MLF lesion is unchanged; fatigable ptosis, positive AChR antibodies and the RNS decrement explain the new signs, and an MS relapse would not cause fatigable proximal and jaw weakness.
High-risk setting (JCV index 3.1, about 3 years of natalizumab), but MRI shows no new subcortical lesion or diffusion abnormality, and the deficits are fatigable and explained by MG.
Normal baseline CMAPs, no significant post-exercise CMAP increment (7%), prominent ocular signs, normal left-sided reflexes and positive AChR antibodies.
The right INO is old and unchanged; INO does not cause ptosis, and the new diplopia is on sustained upgaze.

key_clinical_evidence: New fluctuating bilateral ptosis, diplopia on sustained upgaze, jaw and deltoid fatigue with little response to IV methylprednisolone point to a neuromuscular junction disorder rather than an MS relapse.
Positive ice-pack test on the right eyelid (MRD1 +2.5 mm).
Anti-AChR binding 4.2 nmol/L with elevated blocking and modulating antibodies establishes AChR-positive MG; thyroid function is normal.
RNS decrement of 14% in deltoid and 18% in nasalis with normal baseline CMAPs and no significant post-exercise increment indicates a postsynaptic transmission defect.
Gadolinium brain MRI shows no new or enhancing MS lesion and no imaging features of PML.

Mediastinal CT shows a 2.8 cm well-defined anterior mediastinal mass consistent with thymoma: thymectomy is indicated regardless of MG severity, and the thymoma is a more likely driver of her MG than natalizumab.
The anti-JCV index of 3.1 after about 3 years of natalizumab means MG immunosuppression must not be layered on natalizumab; the MS therapy has to be changed first.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: MS relapses do not produce fatigable ptosis and proximal weakness or an RNS decrement; gadolinium MRI shows no new activity, and AChR antibodies confirm coexisting MG.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute all new neurological symptoms to MS relapse and pursue steroid pulse without considering MG.

sequence_constraints.reason: AChR antibody testing precedes single-fibre EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025).
Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal (Jacob 2025).

interactions: Natalizumab with prednisone or azathioprine: concurrent or prior immunosuppression is a risk factor for natalizumab-associated progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy; the natalizumab label advises against combination with immunosuppressants.
Natalizumab with pyridostigmine: no known interaction.
Sertraline with pyridostigmine, prednisone or azathioprine: no clinically significant interaction.
general.proposed: Pyridostigmine, prednisone, azathioprine (screened against the current medication list)
warnings: Azathioprine: check TPMT (or NUDT15) activity before starting; monitor CBC and liver tests.
Corticosteroids: initial worsening of myasthenic weakness can occur within 1-2 weeks of starting high doses.
Myasthenia gravis: avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium where possible; non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers need reduced doses with quantitative monitoring.

labs.interpretation: Anti-AChR binding 4.2 nmol/L, blocking 48% and modulating 65%, all elevated. Anti-MuSK not detected. Anti-JCV antibody index 3.1 (positive). Thyroid function, CBC and CK within reference ranges. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies are found in a subset of patients with disorders of neuromuscular transmission; clinical correlation recommended.

results.finding: Pyridostigmine is the initial symptomatic treatment; corticosteroids or immunosuppressive therapy are used when goals are not met, and thymectomy is indicated in all patients with thymoma.
results.source: Sanders DB et al. Neurology 2016;87:419-425; update Narayanaswami P et al. Neurology 2021;96:114-122

results.finding: Thymectomy improved clinical outcomes over three years in non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.
results.source: Wolfe GI et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:511-522

results.finding: Natalizumab-associated PML risk rises with anti-JCV antibody index, treatment duration beyond 24 months and prior immunosuppressant use.
results.source: Ho PR et al. Lancet Neurol 2017;16:925-933

myasthenia gravis diagnosis and manageme.summary: Consensus guidance (Sanders DB et al., Neurology 2016;87:419-425; update Narayanaswami P et al., Neurology 2021;96:114-122) recommends AChR antibody testing first, MuSK testing when AChR antibodies are absent, and electrodiagnostic confirmation by repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fibre EMG. Chest CT or MRI is recommended in all patients to detect thymoma. In the MGTX trial (Wolfe GI et al., N Engl J Med 2016;375:511-522) thymectomy improved outcomes over three years in non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65. In natalizumab-treated MS, PML risk increases with the anti-JCV antibody index, exposure beyond 24 months and prior immunosuppression (Ho PR et al., Lancet Neurol 2017;16:925-933).

patient.chief_complaint: New bilateral ptosis and diplopia attributed to possible MS relapse

past_medical_history: Multiple sclerosis (relapsing-remitting, diagnosed 4 years ago, on natalizumab)

patient.history_present_illness: A 38-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis on natalizumab was referred by her MS neurologist and admitted to the neurology service for evaluation of new bilateral ptosis and diplopia over 6 weeks, initially attributed to a possible MS relapse. Her MS neurologist's concern was a new oculomotor finding on top of her prior documented internuclear ophthalmoplegia from an older right MLF lesion. The patient reports the bilateral eyelid drooping began approximately 6 weeks ago, initially intermittent and present mainly in the evenings. She noted double vision, horizontal and worsening on sustained upgaze, that was new and different from her chronic INO-related symptoms. Her last surveillance brain MRI, 8 weeks ago and before these symptoms began, was stable. Her MS neurologist prescribed a 5-day course of high-dose IV methylprednisolone 2 weeks ago for presumed MS relapse, without repeat imaging. The ptosis and diplopia showed minimal improvement with steroids. During and after the course she began to notice mild fatigue when using her arms for overhead activities (hanging laundry, reaching for shelves) and mild difficulty chewing tough meats. She denied significant dysphagia or breathlessness. Her prior MS symptoms (right-sided hemiparesis, cerebellar ataxia, INO) are all at their chronic stable baseline. She has received natalizumab for about 3 years; her most recent anti-JCV antibody index, checked as part of routine natalizumab monitoring, was 3.1. Her MS neurologist found the poor steroid response and the new jaw and arm fatigue unexpected and referred her for further evaluation.

neurological_exam.additional: No dysphagia or dysarthria; no nasal speech. Neck flexion strength normal. Single-breath count not performed.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Right internuclear ophthalmoplegia: right eye adduction deficit with dissociated nystagmus of the abducting left eye on left lateral gaze (prior MS lesion, documented, unchanged). Bilateral ptosis, new, right greater than left, increasing during 60 seconds of sustained upgaze. New diplopia on sustained upgaze. Pupils 4 mm, equal and reactive; no relative afferent pupillary defect. Mild orbicularis oculi weakness bilaterally (eyelashes partly visible on forced eye closure).
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly spastic gait right side (MS). No significant worsening from baseline.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Mild cognitive slowing on formal testing (consistent with known MS). Depressed affect.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild spasticity right upper extremity (chronic MS finding). New proximal upper extremity weakness: deltoids 4-/5 bilaterally, fatigable (worsens on repetition). Chronic right hemiparesis (MS) stable. No new lower extremity weakness.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Right-sided hyperreflexia with a right extensor plantar response (chronic MS finding, unchanged). Left reflexes normal, left plantar flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Prior patchy sensory deficits from MS — unchanged. No new sensory changes.

physical_exam.general: Weight 59.6 kg, height 165 cm. Well appearing, no respiratory distress.
